note: Kuwait. The Ministry of Interior's residence page (moi.gov.kw, General Directorate of Residency Affairs) still links Ministerial Decree 957 of 2019, the executive regulations of the Residence of Foreigners Law of 1959, but the residence law was replaced in 2024 and the Ministry published new executive by-laws in the official gazette (reported as Ministerial Decision 2249 of 2025, in force from 23 December 2025, since amended); their text wasn't found on the Ministry's pages on 2026-10-30, so this file rests on Gulf News's report of the gazette (secondary). Under the new by-laws the renewal fee for standard residencies, which cover private sector workers among others, is KD20 a year (renewable); investors and property owners (Articles 19 and 21) pay KD50 a year, and the new self-sponsored residency (Article 24) KD500 a year (for means). Fees by the year aren't held by the form, so none is kept; the residence's term, decision time, place of application and work rights aren't in the report. The 2019 decree (for the record, read by eye: ordinary residence up to five years, renewable; private sector residence granted on the competent body's work permit and transferable only with its leave) is superseded and isn't written. GCC citizens aren't modelled apart; Kuwait has no permanent residence route here.

sources.title: Gulf News, Kuwait rolls out major hike in residency and visa fees
sources.said: The revised charges, published in the official gazette on Sunday, will take effect one month from now. They are part of the executive by-laws introduced under the updated Residency Law issued last year. ... The renewal fee for standard residencies, covering government employees, private sector workers, foreign students, clergymen and similar categories, has doubled to KD20 per year. ... Residency fees for foreign investors and property owners (Articles 19 and 21) will be KD50 annually, while the newly introduced self-sponsored residency category (Article 24) comes with a steep KD500 annual fee.
